text_blocks.snippet: An exercise stress test evaluates how well your heart functions during physical activity, assessing blood flow to the heart muscle. Normal results indicate your heart is healthy enough for exercise and that there are no significant blood flow problems. Abnormal results, such as ECG changes or symptoms like chest pain during exercise, may suggest potential issues like coronary artery disease and require further investigation.
snippet_highlighted_words: Normal results indicate your heart is healthy enough for exercise and that there are no significant blood flow problems

text_blocks.snippet: What is an Exercise Stress Test?

An exercise stress test, also known as a treadmill test or stress ECG, involves monitoring your heart's electrical activity (using an ECG) and blood pressure while you walk on a treadmill or pedal a stationary bike. The intensity of the exercise gradually increases, simulating the demands placed on your heart during physical activity.

list.title: Normal:
list.snippet: A normal test indicates that your heart is responding appropriately to the increasing demands of exercise, with no significant ECG changes or symptoms like chest pain or shortness of breath. It suggests your heart is healthy and capable of handling physical exertion.
ECG changes: Changes in the ST segment of the ECG, which can indicate reduced blood flow to the heart muscle (ischemia).
Chest pain or other symptoms: The development of chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, or lightheadedness during exercise can also be a sign of abnormal blood flow to the heart.
Blood pressure changes: An inadequate increase or a decrease in blood pressure during exercise can also be an indicator of a problem.
Arrhythmias: The development of abnormal heart rhythms during exercise can also be a cause for concern.

text_blocks.snippet: Abnormal stress test results can suggest several potential issues, including:

list.title: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD):
list.snippet: This is the most common condition associated with abnormal stress test results, where fatty deposits (plaques) build up in the arteries and restrict blood flow to the heart.

list.title: Heart rhythm problems (arrhythmias):
list.snippet: The test can reveal if you have abnormal heart rhythms during exercise, which may require further investigation.

list.title: Other heart conditions:
list.snippet: The test can also provide information about other potential heart conditions that may require attention.

text_blocks.snippet: If your stress test results are normal, your doctor may advise you to continue your current exercise routine or lifestyle and schedule follow-up appointments as needed. If the results are abnormal, your doctor may recommend further tests, such as a coronary angiogram, which can visualize blockages in the heart arteries, or a nuclear stress test, which provides more detailed information about blood flow to the heart.
